problem_type: Retargeted Director actions pass joint-angle checks while the character's whole pose is wrong
symptom: Push_Loop and Death01 passed the second-round angle checker even though the contact sheet showed the target hovering or standing while the source was bent or lying down.
direct_cause: The previous X Bot conversion and metric normalized each character by its hip-to-head frame and applied locomotion contact checks only to selected actions, so whole-body stance errors were cancelled or ignored.
class_root: The default 3D-BOX actor must keep the source library's native mesh, skeleton, and action clips together; no X Bot retargeted derivative can enter the native UAL catalog.
affected_population: All 45 Quaternius Universal Animation Library actions
Future Director planner selections that consume the native action catalog
The old X Bot/Mixamo director path, which remains a separate legacy surface
internal_only_reason: The source-vs-target choice is an application asset policy; the third-party archive supplies the content and license but does not decide which actor the Director catalog owns.
invariants: The catalog has exactly 45 native UAL clips and every clip name exists in the same GLB as the UAL skeleton.
The GLB contains the UAL semantic bones, one neutral UAL_WhiteModel material, no source images or textures, and a ground-min-z origin.
The planner projection exposes only compact identity and semantic fields; runtime cutover is deferred to a separate PR.
Every standing-class action has a deterministic first-frame foot and hip check; crouch, fall, sit, jump, swim, roll, kneel, pickup, push, driving, and low sword poses are explicitly exempt.

door_reduction.why_not: Catalog projection and DevLab rendering are independent consumers of the same native asset contract; both remain required so a stale planner projection cannot masquerade as a visual inspection.

generality_proof: Every UAL action is emitted by one preparation command, checked against one GLB manifest, and registered by mapping the same UAL_ACTIONS list into the catalog. Removing the old retarget path prevents another action from entering through an alternate derivative or stale license record.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Extract the registered UAL GLB, strip source materials, retain native actions, and emit one deterministic manifest.
Fail closed when action count, semantic bones, manifest hashes, or source-material stripping do not match the native UAL contract.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The catalog is generated only from the checked native action list and one UAL GLB file.
The visual inspection page consumes the same catalog file and clipName; no X Bot or FBX fallback remains for action entries.

recurrence.reason: Any future derivative conversion or stale catalog entry could reintroduce the same whole-body mismatch unless the native file and clip-name contract is checked at the shared asset boundary.

prevention.invariant: Only the one checked UAL GLB may back the 45 action catalog entries, with all semantic bones and no source textures.
prevention.failure_mode: The checker exits non-zero for missing actions, bones, hash drift, unexpected materials, or texture payloads; catalog checks fail for missing or unlicensed binaries.
prevention.strategy: Keep source processing, manifest hashes, semantic mapping, standing checks, and visual inspection on the native asset boundary; delete the old derivative path in the same PR.

legacy_paths.rationale: The obsolete retarget paths were deleted in the preceding unit commit; no legacy runtime path remains in this native UAL asset contract.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Blender is retained only as the offline UAL archive processor; the packaged application has no Blender runtime dependency.
dependency_lifecycle.target: A pinned Blender release or a repository-owned glTF sanitizer that reproduces the same output hash and animation manifest
exit_criteria: A replacement emits the same 45 action names, semantic bones, material stripping, and ground measurement.
Two runs on the conversion host and CI emit byte-identical GLB output.

migration: No user scene migration is needed because runtime cutover is intentionally deferred. The future switch PR will select the UAL GLB for new 3D-BOX scenes while leaving old X Bot/Mixamo scenes untouched.
residual_risks: The UAL native actor is cataloged but not yet wired into actionLibrary.ts or the existing Director runtime; that is an explicit later switch PR.
Visual inspection uses Blender-generated contact sheets and the existing DevLab page; browser-packaged runtime loading is not claimed by this asset-only PR.
